claims.text: Mechanical surface polishing will delay or suppress localized corrosion initiation on pre-exposure Q235 steel in chloride-containing environments.
The proposed polishing benefit will occur at both room and elevated temperatures.
As-received Q235 steel contains surface-accessible inclusions.
As-received Q235 steel contains grain-boundary irregularities relevant to corrosion initiation.
As-received Q235 steel has a native surface oxide layer.
Mechanical polishing removes surface irregularities and inclusions from Q235 steel.
Mechanical polishing can remove the proposed surface defects while maintaining the bulk properties of Q235 steel.
Surface heterogeneities can produce localized anodic and cathodic regions during corrosion in 3.5 wt.% NaCl.
Inclusions and grain-boundary sites on untreated Q235 steel act as localized anodic regions for corrosion initiation.
Chloride exposure causes untreated Q235 surface heterogeneities to function as preferential sites for localized galvanic corrosion.
Polishing produces a more uniform and potentially more protective oxide layer on Q235 steel.
A more uniform oxide layer retards the initiation and progression of pitting or other localized corrosion on Q235 steel.
Polished Q235 steel will have a lower corrosion rate than unpolished Q235 steel under otherwise identical chloride exposure.
Polished Q235 steel will have a lower pitting density than unpolished Q235 steel.
Polished Q235 steel will have a more noble corrosion potential than unpolished Q235 steel.
The magnitude of the polishing benefit depends on the initial defect density and polishing effectiveness.
The stability of the oxide film formed after polishing may vary at elevated temperature.
